claim: NaLi-H1 is the first fully synthetic phage display library of humanized llama single domain antibody.
source: Here, we describe the first fully synthetic phage display library of humanized llama single domain antibody (NaLi-H1: Nanobody Library Humanized 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a primary contribution of the work.

claim: NaLi-H1 is based on a humanized synthetic single domain antibody (hs2dAb) scaffold optimized for intracellular stability.
source: Based on a humanized synthetic single domain antibody (hs2dAb) scaffold optimized for intracellular stability, the highly diverse library provides high affinity binders without animal immunization.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the library is based on an hs2dAb scaffold optimized for intracellular stability.

claim: NaLi-H1 provides high affinity binders without animal immunization.
source: Based on a humanized synthetic single domain antibody (hs2dAb) scaffold optimized for intracellular stability, the highly diverse library provides high affinity binders without animal immunization.
evidence: The abstract states that the library provides high affinity binders without requiring animal immunization.

claim: NaLi-H1 was screened against various targets including Fluorescent proteins, actin, tubulin, p53, and HP1.
source: NaLi-H1 was screened following several selection schemes against various targets (Fluorescent proteins, actin, tubulin, p53, HP1).
evidence: The abstract explicitly lists the targets against which the library was screened.

claim: Conformation antibodies against active RHO GTPase were obtained from NaLi-H1.
source: Conformation antibodies against active RHO GTPase were also obtained.
evidence: The abstract states that conformation-specific antibodies against active RHO GTPase were obtained.

claim: Selected hs2dAb were used in various immunoassays.
source: Selected hs2dAb were used in various immunoassays and were often found to be functional intrabodies, enabling tracking or inhibition of endogenous targets.
evidence: The abstract states that selected hs2dAb were used in various immunoassays.

claim: Selected hs2dAb were often found to be functional intrabodies.
source: Selected hs2dAb were used in various immunoassays and were often found to be functional intrabodies, enabling tracking or inhibition of endogenous targets.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that selected hs2dAb were often functional intrabodies.

claim: Functionalization of intrabodies allowed specific protein knockdown in living cells.
source: Functionalization of intrabodies allowed specific protein knockdown in living cells.
evidence: The abstract states that functionalized intrabodies enabled protein knockdown in living cells.

claim: Direct selection against the surface of tumor cells produced hs2dAb directed against tumor-specific antigens.
source: Finally, direct selection against the surface of tumor cells produced hs2dAb directed against tumor-specific antigens further highlighting the potential use of this library for therapeutic applications.
evidence: The abstract states that selection against tumor cell surfaces yielded antibodies against tumor-specific antigens.

claim: Antibodies have expanded as the biochemical tools of choice to label antigens in cells or tissues.
source: Antibodies expended as the biochemical tools of choice to label antigens in cells or tissues.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Recombinant methods have been developed over the past 20 years to quickly select and improve monoclonal antibodies from highly diverse libraries.
source: Over the past 20 years, recombinant methods have been developed to quickly select and improve monoclonal antibodies from highly diverse libraries.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Immune libraries provide in general high affinity binders but diversity is sometimes limited.
source: Immune libraries provide in general high affinity binders but, depending on the antigen, diversity is sometimes limited.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about immune libraries.

claim: Natural antibody selection requires animal immunization.
source: Because natural antibody selection requires animal immunization, very conserved or toxic antigens should be avoided and, in general, only limited control of the immune response is possible.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of natural antibody selection.

claim: Non-immune (naïve) libraries provide a higher diversity of binders even for antigens highly conserved in mammals.
source: On the contrary, non-immune (naïve) libraries provide a higher diversity of binders even for antigens highly conserved in mammals, but high specificity and affinity can be reached only when selecting from very large functional libraries.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of naïve libraries.

claim: The smallest IgG portion capable of binding with high specificity an antigen is the Fv fragment consisting of the variable heavy (VH) and the variable light (VL) domains.
source: The smallest IgG portion capable of binding with high specificity an antigen is the Fv fragment consisting of the variable heavy (VH) and the variable light (VL) domains.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about antibody structure.

claim: In the case of single domain antibodies (sdAb), a VH or a VL alone is able to bind its target antigen.
source: In the case of single domain antibodies (sdAb), a VH or a VL alone, is able to bind its target antigen.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of single domain antibodies.

claim: Each variable domain contains four conserved framework regions (FRW or framework) and three regions called CDR (Complementarity Determining Regions).
source: Each variable domain contains four conserved framework regions (FRW or framework) and three regions called CDR (Complementarity Determining Regions) corresponding to hypervariable sequences which determine the specificity for the antigen.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about antibody structure.

claim: CDRs correspond to hypervariable sequences which determine the specificity for the antigen.
source: Each variable domain contains four conserved framework regions (FRW or framework) and three regions called CDR (Complementarity Determining Regions) corresponding to hypervariable sequences which determine the specificity for the antigen.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about CDR function.

claim: Antibodies called HCAb in Camelidae have an antigen recognition part composed of only a VH domain.
source: Interestingly, antibodies called HCAb in Camelidae (Hamers-Casterman et al., 1993) or IgNAR in sharks (Greenberg et al., 1995) have an antigen recognition part composed of only a VH domain.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Camelid natural single domain VH are referred to as VHH or nanobodies.
source: Camelid natural single domain VH, referred to as VHH or nanobodies, can be expressed as recombinant fragments and represent attractive alternatives over classical antibody fragments like scFvs because they are easy to manipulate and they are not limited by potential misfolding of the two domains (Wörn and Plückthun, 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established nomenclature with citation.

claim: VHH FRWs show a high sequence and structural homology with human VH domains of family III.
source: It is noteworthy that VHH FRWs show a high sequence and structural homology with human VH domains of family III (Muyldermans, 2013) and VHH have comparable immunogenicity as human VH (Bartunek et al., 2013; Holz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: VHH have comparable immunogenicity as human VH.
source: It is noteworthy that VHH FRWs show a high sequence and structural homology with human VH domains of family III (Muyldermans, 2013) and VHH have comparable immunogenicity as human VH (Bartunek et al., 2013; Holz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Some nanobodies are currently in phase II and Phase III clinical trials.
source: Thus, they further constitute very interesting agents for therapeutic applications, some of them are currently in phase II and Phase III clinical trials (Ablynx Nanobodies; http://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/results?term=ablynx).
evidence: This is stated with reference to clinical trial data.

claim: Production of functional intrabodies depends on the stability of the antibody fragments in the reducing environment of the cytosol.
source: Production of functional intrabodies depends on the stability of the antibody fragments in the reducing environment of the cytosol that does not allow disulfide bond formation between conserved cysteine.
evidence: This is stated as a known requirement for intrabody function.

claim: The nanobody scaffold has higher solubility compared to other antibody formats.
source: In this context, many advantages of the nanobody scaffold have been reported and, in particular, higher solubility, improved stability in a reducing environment (Wesolowski et al., 2009), as well as higher expression yield and thermostability (Jobling et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: The nanobody scaffold has improved stability in a reducing environment.
source: In this context, many advantages of the nanobody scaffold have been reported and, in particular, higher solubility, improved stability in a reducing environment (Wesolowski et al., 2009), as well as higher expression yield and thermostability (Jobling et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: A family of highly functional VHH scaffolds was isolated using a fusion assay in E. coli.
source: First, using a fusion assay in E. coli, a family of highly functional VHH scaffolds was isolated, optimized for intracellular expression and high stability.
evidence: This is stated as a method used in the study.

claim: One particularly stable VHH scaffold consensus sequence was chosen from selected antibodies.
source: One particularly stable VHH scaffold consensus sequence was chosen from these selected antibodies.
evidence: This is stated as a step in the library design process.

claim: Additional changes were introduced to reduce the distance between the Camelidae and human VH3 sequences.
source: Additional changes were then introduced to reduce the distance between the Camelidae and human VH3 sequences.
evidence: This is stated as a design step for humanization.

claim: The humanized synthetic scaffold (hs2dAb) was confirmed to be robust and functional by CDR grafting.
source: We confirmed by CDR grafting that this humanized synthetic scaffold (hs2dAb) was robust and functional.
evidence: This is stated as a validation step in the study.

claim: The NaLi-H1 library has a diversity of 3.10^9 independent hs2dAb.
source: Statistics of amino-acid diversity in the CDRs were computed and these information were used to construct a high diversity phage display library of 3.109 independent hs2dAb.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the constructed library.

claim: Highly specific antibodies were selected against EGFP, mCherry, β-tubulin, β-actin, heterochromatin protein HP1α, GTP-bound RHO, p53 and HER2.
source: Highly specific antibodies were selected against EGFP, mCherry, β-tubulin, β-actin, heterochromatin protein HP1α, GTP-bound RHO, p53 and HER2.
evidence: This is stated as a result of library screening.

claim: Affinity measurement indicated that affinities in the nM range can be obtained using this library.
source: Affinity measurement indicated that affinities in the nM range can be obtained using this library.
evidence: This is stated as a result of affinity measurements.

claim: hs2dAb are frequently usable as fluorescent intrabodies to track antigens in cells.
source: As expected from our design, we further showed that hs2dAb are frequently usable as fluorescent intrabodies to track antigens in cells.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability of the hs2dAb.

claim: hs2dAb can be functionalized to induce antigen knockdown.
source: We also showed that they can be functionalized to induce antigen knockdown.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability of the hs2dAb.

claim: This is the first report of a large and diverse synthetic single domain antibody library enabling fully in vitro selection of highly functional antibodies and intrabodies.
source: This thus represents the first report of a large and diverse synthetic single domain antibody library enabling fully in vitro selection of highly functional antibodies and intrabodies.
evidence: This is stated as the primary contribution of the work.

claim: The consensus scaffold was matching the sequence of the most robust VHH framework, represented by a single domain antibody D10 (sdAbD10).
source: Strikingly, the consensus scaffold was matching the sequence of the most robust VHH framework, represented by a single domain antibody D10 (hereafter named sdAbD10).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the scaffold selection process.

claim: sdAbD10 provided higher antibiotic resistance in the chloramphenicol filter assay compared to previously reported thermostable nanobodies or intrabodies.
source: When compared to previously reported thermostable nanobodies (Olichon et al., 2007a) or intrabodies (Rothbauer et al., 2006) obtained from immune libraries, sdAbD10 was found to provide higher antibiotic resistance in the chloramphenicol filter assay (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing comparative data.

claim: sdAbD10 expression yield in E.coli periplasm was in the higher range of soluble llama VHH fragments.
source: Its expression yield in E.coli periplasm was in the higher range of soluble llama VHH fragments, allowing efficient and quantitative purification (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Purified sdAbD10 showed excellent solubility and stability after treatment at 70°C.
source: Purified sdAbD10 showed excellent solubility, stability after treatment at 70°C and we did not observe aggregation when expressed as an intrabody fused to the EGFP in mammalian cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Seven residues of the synthetic scaffold sdAbD10 were altered towards the most represented in human VH3.
source: Seven residues of the synthetic scaffold sdAbD10 were altered towards the most represented in human VH3 while five other divergent residues were kept unchanged.
evidence: This is stated as part of the humanization process.

claim: The four llama VHH-specific amino acids hallmarks in the framework-2 region (positions 42, 49, 50, and 52) were maintained in the hs2dAb scaffold.
source: The four llama VHH-specific amino acids hallmarks in the framework-2 region (positions 42, 49, 50, and 52), which are essential to increase intrinsic solubility properties, as well as the Glutamine in position 103, were maintained.
evidence: This is stated as a design decision for the hs2dAb scaffold.

claim: Both the sdAbD10 and hs2dAb scaffolds enabled functional display of the grafted CDRs.
source: Importantly, both the sdAbD10 and hs2dAb scaffolds enabled functional display of the grafted CDRs and robust detection of endogenous lamin was observed by immunofluorescence staining of Hela cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2C showing immunofluorescence data.

claim: Both the hs2dAb and the sdAbD10 scaffolds allowed the efficient intrabody use of the synthetic anti-lamin antibodies.
source: Similarly, we observed that both the hs2dAb and the sdAbD10 scaffolds allowed the efficient intrabody use of the synthetic anti-lamin antibodies (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: A constant length of 7 amino acids was selected for CDR1 and CDR2.
source: A constant length of 7 amino acids was selected for CDR1 and CDR2.
evidence: This is stated as a design decision for the library.

claim: Four different lengths of CDR3 (9, 12, 15 or 18 amino acids) were chosen to cover the spectrum of natural VHH CDR3 length.
source: Thus, we chose to use four different lengths of CDR3 to cover this spectrum (9, 12, 15 or and 18 amino acids) and introduce random amino acid (except cysteine) at each position.
evidence: This is stated as a design decision for the library.

claim: About 3×10^9 individual recombinant hs2dAb clones were obtained.
source: About 3.109 individual recombinant hs2dAb clones were obtained.
evidence: This is stated as the size of the library obtained.

claim: Only 13 out of 315 randomly sequenced clones were found to be incorrect, representing about 4% of potential defects.
source: We first evaluated the quality of the NaLi-H1 library by sequencing 315 random clones. Only 13 sequences were found to be incorrect (bearing an in-frame stop codon, missing one base, missing a large region [the CDR1 or CDR1-FWR1- CDR2], or being empty). Thus, a total of about 4% of potential default was observed, which is rather low and only marginal in comparison to the 3.109 clones obtained.
evidence: This is stated as a quality control result.

claim: The four CDR3 lengths (9, 12, 15 or 18 amino acids) were present in similar proportions in the library.
source: This confirmed the quality of the library and showed that the four CDR3 lengths (9, 12, 15 or and 18 amino acids) were present in similar proportions.
evidence: This is stated as a result of next generation sequencing analysis.

claim: All 24 randomly picked clones tested showed essentially complete solubility after centrifugation at 250,000 g.
source: To estimate the overall folding of the hs2dAb present in the library, we picked randomly 24 clones and tested their solubility in bacteria medium after secretion. Medium were centrifuged at 250 000 g and the supernatant and pellet were analyzed. All tested clones showed essentially complete solubility, at least as good as a natural Lama antibody (GFP4).
evidence: This is stated as a result of solubility testing.

claim: After warming at 90°C for 10 min, the hs2dAb showed good solubility (over 70%).
source: Even after warming at 90°C for 10 min, the hs2dAb showed good solubility (over 70%) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: From the panning against EGFP, 37 non redundant nanobodies were shown to detect EGFP by phage ELISA.
source: From the panning against EGFP, 37 non redundant nanobodies were shown to detect EGFP by phage ELISA.
evidence: This is stated as a result of screening against EGFP.

claim: 10 out of 37 anti-EGFP antibodies were found to efficiently stain EGFP in fixed HeLa cells.
source: These antibodies were then used for immunofluorescence and 10 of them were found to efficiently stain EGFP in fixed HeLa cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2A showing immunofluorescence data.

claim: Selection against mCherry led to 6 positive binders.
source: Similarly, selection against mCherry led to 6 positive binders (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: After two rounds of selection against tubulin, 3 out of 40 clones analyzed were shown to detect endogenous tubulin by immunofluorescence.
source: After two rounds of selection, 3 out of 40 clones analyzed were shown to detect endogenous tubulin by immunofluorescence (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: A screen against coated β-actin led to the identification of 16 unique binders positive in phage ELISA.
source: A screen against coated β-actin led to the identification of 16 unique binders positive in phage ELISA.
evidence: This is stated as a result of screening against β-actin.

claim: Seven anti-actin antibodies decorated endogenous actin stress fibers by immunofluorescence in MRC5 cells.
source: Seven of these antibodies decorated endogenous actin stress fibers by immunofluorescence in MRC5 cells (Figure 2D) as well as in other cell lines.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: Three of the anti-actin hs2dAb detected a single band at the molecular weight of β-actin in western blot from HeLa cell extract.
source: Three of the hs2dAb detected a single band at the molecular weight of β-actin in western blot from HeLa cell extract while one of the anti-tubulin detected a band at the correct molecular weight of tubulin (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Among 12 clones positive in phage ELISA against p53, 6 selected hs2dAb were shown to label endogenous p53 in immunofluorescence on A431 cells.
source: Among 12 clones positive in phage ELISA, 6 selected hs2dAb were shown to label endogenous p53 in immunofluorescence on A431 cells (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 2E.

claim: 5 individual hs2dAb against HP1α were directly identified by immunofluorescence staining of HeLa cells.
source: 5 individual hs2dAb were directly identified by immunofluorescence staining of HeLa cells.
evidence: This is stated as a result of screening against HP1α.

claim: After four rounds of selection against RHOA, one antibody (H12) represented more than 50% of the population.
source: After four rounds of selection, clones were analyzed using phage ELISA against either wild type RHOA loaded with GTPγS (a non-hydrolysable analogue of GTP) or GDP-loaded RHOA. Forty clones presenting a differential ELISA signal in favor of the GTP loaded RHOA were sequenced. One antibody, represented by clone H12, represented more than 50% of the population.
evidence: This is stated as a result of screening against RHOA.

claim: H12 recognized the constitutively active mutant RHOA L63 (RHOA-CA) which is bound to GTP.
source: H12 recognized the constitutively active mutant RHOA L63 (RHOA-CA) which is bound to GTP due to impaired hydrolysis activity.
evidence: This is stated as a result of ELISA analysis.

claim: H12 showed no binding to the dominant negative RHOA N19 mutant RHOA-DN nor to GDP-loaded wild type RHOA.
source: In contrast, no binding was observed to the dominant negative RHOA N19 mutant RHOA-DN nor to GDP-loaded wild type RHOA (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3A showing ELISA data.

claim: The H12 hs2dAb was found to be highly selective of RHO loaded with GTPγS as it was unable to precipitate RHO from GDP loaded extract.
source: The H12 hs2dAb was found to be highly selective of RHO loaded with GTPγS as it was unable to precipitate RHO from GDP loaded extract (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3B showing pull-down data.

claim: H12 staining was correlated with the level of GFP-RHOA CA mutant expression.
source: In contrast, a staining with H12 was correlated with the level of GFP-RHOA CA mutant expression.
evidence: This is stated as a result of immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: After the third round of bio-panning against SKBR3 cells, 88 clones were analyzed by FACS and 58 were found to be positive when tested on SKBR3 cells and negative on MCF7 cells.
source: After the third round of bio-panning, 88 clones were analyzed by FACS and 58 were found to be positive when tested on SKBR3 cells and negative on MCF7 cells.
evidence: This is stated as a result of cell surface selection.

claim: Sequencing the 58 positive clones revealed that 15 independent binders had been selected.
source: Sequencing the 58 positive clones revealed that 15 independent binders had been selected.
evidence: This is stated as a result of sequencing analysis.

claim: 12 out of 15 clones recognized HER2 exoplasmic domain by ELISA using HER2-Fc as a target antigen.
source: Although the subtractive selection was not performed on identical cell lines expressing or not HER2, we observed strikingly that 12 clones out of 15 recognized HER2 exoplasmic domain by ELISA using HER2-Fc as a target antigen (Figure 3E), suggesting that it behaves as a dominant differential epitope.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 3E showing ELISA data.

claim: Most of the hs2dAbs tested gave a monodispersed fluorescence when fused to a fluorescent protein and observed in living cells.
source: Randomly chosen hs2dAbs were fused to a fluorescent protein and observed in living cells. In comparison to our previous experience with scFv or nanobody libraries in which a majority of tested antibodies showed aggregation when expressed in the cytosol as an EGFP-fusion, most of the hs2dAbs tested here gave a monodispersed fluorescence, and very few were showing aggregates.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from intrabody expression experiments.

claim: Several anti-GFP and anti-mCherry hs2dAbs were found to efficiently label their targets in living cells.
source: In contrast, several anti-GFP and anti-mCherry hs2dAbs were found to efficiently label their targets, like for example GFP-Rab6 or Myr-Palm-mCherry fusion proteins, in living cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4A showing intrabody localization.

claim: The anti-p53 hs2dAb fused to mCherry were clearly accumulated in the nucleus of SKBR3 cells where endogenous p53 is also localized.
source: Similarly, the anti-p53 hs2dAb fused to mCherry were clearly accumulated in the nucleus of SKBR3 cells where endogenous p53 is also localized.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from intrabody expression experiments.

claim: Anti-HP1 expressed as an EGFP tagged protein in HeLa cells localized in the nucleus where it labels condensed structures similar to HP1 usual staining.
source: Figure 4C (lower panel) shows that anti-HP1 expressed as an EGFP tagged protein in HeLa cells localized in the nucleus where it labels condensed structures similar to HP1 usual staining.
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 4C showing intrabody localization.

claim: H12 was able to perturb endogenous RHO activity when expressed in the cytosol.
source: Intrabodies may allow not only to track the dynamics of their cellular target, but also to perturb, or block, their activity. Our results indeed indicate that the H12 antibody was able to perturb endogenous RHO activity when expressed in the cytosol.
evidence: This is stated as a result of functional analysis.

claim: H12 was pulled-down by RHOA CA but not by inactive RHOA DN in co-immunoprecipitation experiments.
source: H12 carrying a carboxy-terminal myc tag was expressed in HeLa cells together with either the CBD-fused RHOA DN or with the CBD-RHOA CA mutants. H12 was pulled-down by RHOA CA but not by inactive RHOA DN (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1 showing co-IP data.

claim: Cells expressing H12-EGFP were totally devoid of actin stress fibers.
source: In contrast to un-transfected cells or cells transfected with various non-relevant EGFP fused hs2dAb (Figure 5A, upper panel), we observed that cells expressing H12-EGFP were totally devoid of actin stress fibers (Figure 5A, lower panel).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5A showing the phenotypic effect.

claim: F-GFP4 (degradFP) induced a strong reduction of H2B-EGFP expression.
source: As expected, F-GFP4, also known as degradFP, induced a strong reduction of H2B-EGFP expression as analyzed by western blot (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 2 showing western blot data.

claim: Some anti-EGFP clones selected from the NaLi-H1 library failed to degrade H2B-EGFP when expressed as F-Ib.
source: When anti-EGFP clones selected from the NaLi-H1 library were tested, we observed that some of the hs2dAb that were found to active as fluorescent intrabodies failed to degrade H2B-EGFP when expressed as F-Ib.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from protein knockdown experiments.

claim: Several hs2dAb anti-EGFP induced a complete disappearance of nuclear H2B-EGFP signal when expressed as F-Ib.
source: However, several hs2dAb anti-EGFP induced a complete disappearance of nuclear H2B-EGFP signal when expressed as F-Ib (F-R3TF3, Figure 5B) while no reduction was observed when using an anti-EGFP that cannot be used as an intrabody (F-R3TG4, Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5B showing protein knockdown.

claim: FACS analysis showed a decreased of fluorescence intensity by as much as 70% with F-R3TF3.
source: FACS analysis showed a decreased of fluorescence intensity by as much as 70% (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5C showing FACS data.

claim: The protein knockdown effect was reversed in the presence of a proteasome inhibitor.
source: As expected, this effect was reversed in the presence of a proteasome inhibitor (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated with reference to Figure 5D showing the effect of proteasome inhibition.

claim: The hs2dAb displays partial resistance and/or refolding after treatment for 10 min at 90°C.
source: Our data indicate that the hs2dAb displays partial resistance and/or refolding after treatment for 10 min at 90°C.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the hs2dAb scaffold.

claim: Affinity measurements done by surface plasmon resonance revealed KD values in the order of 10 nanomolar and up to 50 picomolar.
source: Affinity measurements done by surface plasmon resonance revealed KD values in the order of 10 nanomolar and up to 50 picomolar.
evidence: This is stated as a result of affinity measurements.

claim: The NaLi-H1 library enables the rapid selection of diverse and highly functional binders.
source: The NaLi-H1 library thus enables the rapid selection of diverse and highly functional binders.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the screening results.

claim: The NaLi-H1 library does not depend on animal experimentation.
source: Because it is a fully synthetic, non immune, library, it does not depend on animal experimentation, it is not limited by natural immunogenicity or toxicity of antigens and allows to develop and adjust the selection without ethic consideration.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the synthetic library approach.

claim: Almost every hs2dAb antibody expressed in mammalian cytosol showed no sign of aggregation.
source: Almost every hs2dAb antibodies we expressed in mammalian cytosol showed no sign of aggregation, which further supported the idea that the synthetic scaffold we designed is robust and highly resistant to reduction.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from intrabody expression experiments.

claim: Without using particular selection schemes, functional intrabodies were frequently obtained from the NaLi-H1 library.
source: Using the NaLi-H1 library, we observed that without using particular selection schemes, functional intrabodies were frequently obtained.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the NaLi-H1 library.

claim: NaLi-H1 can provide highly functional hs2dAb which appeared as good as intrabodies from immune libraries.
source: Although we did not formally compare the NaLi-H1 library to previous llama naïve or semi synthetic libraries, the functionality of selected hs2dAb was compared to a sub-nanomolar affinity intrabody, the GFP4 nanobody, which has been extensively used (Caussinus et al., 2011; Kirchhofer et al., 2010). We observed by monitoring its signal-to-noise ratio and by using it in a protein knockdown assay that NaLi-H1 can provide highly functional hs2dAb which appeared as good as intrabodies from immune libraries.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with established intrabodies.
